decisions.reason: The splash-control decision does not determine whisk material, style, size, or positioning; the separate whisk uncertainty from this message is already represented.
Minimal splashing is a separate operating constraint and does not change the candidate's desired smoothness, froth, consistency, or foam-quality state.
A possible splash guard or bowl lip does not necessarily change food-path cleaning behavior; the message's separate bowl-cleaning requirement is already represented.
The splash-control modification concerns splashing during mixing; the message's separate dispensing-flow and no-sputtering changes are already represented.
The conditional use of a splash guard or lip does not change the selected bowl capacity, deep-well form, or compact-size preference.
The source does not specify an enclosure-size or profile change, and the conditional splash-control methods do not necessarily alter the enclosure state.
Splash-control behavior has no effect on the beige primary color or green accent requirements.
The mixing splash constraint does not change the DJ-turntable visual theme.
Although splash control supports practical event use, the source does not change the candidate's general repeated-operation reliability requirement.
The splash-control modification does not change the spout's location, orientation, geometry reference, or fabrication style.
The conditional splash guard or bowl lip does not necessarily change the V1 component-sourcing strategy or the already selected custom spout strategy.
The message reaffirms the existing solenoid approach and existing no-drip closed-state behavior rather than changing them; the splash-control modification adds no new control semantics.
